$comment: What a request may carry before it reaches the OPC UA server (issue #139), driven through BOTH runtimes: tests/unit/test_request_limits.py and packages/server-node/test/request-limits.test.mjs read this file and assert the same verdict and the same sentence. `requests` runs each call through everything that happens before the network — the request-wide bounds (limits.ts / limits.py, checkRequestBounds) and then the contract schema, whose maxItems carries the per-tool counts — in that order, so a case can also pin which rule answers first. `error` is the exact message, from contract/tools.json -> errors; null means the call is accepted. Strings, arrays and nesting too large to write out are built from three directives both suites expand identically: {"$string": N} is N copies of 'a', and {"$string": [N, "é"]} N copies of that character; {"$array": [ITEM, N]} is N copies of ITEM, itself expanded; {"$nest": [N, LEAF]} is LEAF inside N single-element arrays. The numbers are written out rather than derived, so a change to a limit has to change this table on purpose — `limits` below is compared with the contract to make sure it does. The request-size cases are sized exactly: 8 write entries of {"node_id":"a","value":"<s>"} are 227 bytes of JSON plus the strings, so strings summing to 1048349 bytes make a request of exactly 1048576. `byteStrings` is the one limit that applies after conversion, in the variant codec, because a ByteString's size is only known once its base64 is decoded. `eventBufferSizes` is the clamp subscribe_events applies.

requests.name: a string exactly at the limit is accepted
one byte over the string limit is refused, naming where it is
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes argument nodes[0].value is a string of 131073 bytes, over the 131072-byte limit on one string (limits.maxStringBytes). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: the string limit counts bytes, not characters
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes argument nodes[0].value is a string of 131074 bytes, over the 131072-byte limit on one string (limits.maxStringBytes). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a node id is a string like any other
requests.error: read_opcua_nodes argument node_ids[1] is a string of 131073 bytes, over the 131072-byte limit on one string (limits.maxStringBytes). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a read-only tool is bounded too
requests.error: browse_opcua_nodes argument name_filter is a string of 131073 bytes, over the 131072-byte limit on one string (limits.maxStringBytes). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: an array value exactly at the item limit is accepted
an array value one item over the limit is refused
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes argument nodes[0].value has 10001 items, over the 10000-item limit on one array (limits.maxArrayItems). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a huge list is refused on its length, before the schema looks at a single element
requests.error: read_opcua_nodes argument node_ids has 20000 items, over the 10000-item limit on one array (limits.maxArrayItems). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a value nested to exactly the depth limit is accepted
one level deeper is refused at the level that crossed it
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes argument nodes[0].value[0][0][0][0][0] nests arrays or objects more than 8 levels deep, counting the arguments themselves (limits.maxNestingDepth). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a pathologically deep value is refused at the same place, not walked to the bottom
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes argument nodes[0].value[0][0][0][0][0] nests arrays or objects more than 8 levels deep, counting the arguments themselves (limits.maxNestingDepth). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: an argument the tool does not have is bounded before it is named
requests.error: read_opcua_nodes argument junk[0][0][0][0][0][0][0] nests arrays or objects more than 8 levels deep, counting the arguments themselves (limits.maxNestingDepth). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a request of exactly the byte limit is accepted
one byte over the request limit is refused, though every string is within its own
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes arguments are 1048577 bytes of JSON, over the 1048576-byte limit on one request (limits.maxRequestBytes). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

requests.name: a write batch at the per-call limit is accepted
one write over the per-call limit refuses the whole batch
requests.error: write_opcua_nodes accepts at most 100 entries in nodes, got 101. Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server; split the request.

requests.name: a batch read at the per-call limit is accepted
one node over the batch-read limit
requests.error: read_opcua_nodes accepts at most 500 entries in node_ids, got 501. Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server; split the request.

requests.name: a method call at the argument limit is accepted
one method argument over the limit
requests.error: call_opcua_method accepts at most 64 entries in arguments, got 65. Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server; split the request.

byteStrings.name: a ByteString exactly at the limit converts
one byte over is refused, whatever the write would have done
byteStrings.error: A ByteString of 65537 bytes is over the 65536-byte limit on one ByteString value (limits.maxByteStringBytes). Nothing was sent to the OPC UA server.

eventBufferSizes.name: zero is the default, not a buffer that keeps nothing
a size within the limit is kept
past the limit is clamped to it
an absurd size is clamped, not allocated
